title: TxQueue.complete() removes by value-equality instead of entry identity
description: tx_queue.py:523: self._entries.remove(entry) deletes the first value-equal TxQueueEntry (plain @dataclass __eq__), not necessarily the reserved object. fail() (567) and cancel_reservation() (579) already use identity; complete() is the one inconsistent site. Unreachable today (complete is only called on the reserved head while the queue cannot mutate under _tx_lock), but a byte-identical entry pushed to the head while a twin is in flight (lock-bypassing push, same-ms enqueue_time_ms) would remove the wrong object and leave the stale twin eligible to re-reserve -> duplicate transmission. Fix: identity scan (e.g. next(i for i,e in enumerate(self._entries) if e is entry)) mirroring fail()/cancel_reservation(). Related: project-LICHEN-worker6-gwpt. Found by correctness codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-9qpz.
close_reason: Fixed complete() in python/src/lichen/link/tx_queue.py: value-equality self._entries.remove(entry) replaced with identity scan (next(i for i,e in enumerate(self._entries) if e is entry) + del), mirroring fail()/cancel_reservation() identity semantics; success/failure paths, stats, EMA, and idempotent reservation signaling preserved. Test-first with independent oracle: new test_complete_removes_exact_reserved_entry_not_value_twin constructs a byte-identical twin inserted ahead of the reserved entry and asserts the reserved object is removed and the twin survives - verified RED on pre-fix code (twin was removed instead) and GREEN post-fix. tests/link/test_tx_queue.py 95 passed, test_link_tx.py 31 passed. ruff check clean on touched files; the file's pre-existing ruff-format drift and 2 strict-mypy errors (lines 96-164, 291) verified pre-existing via git stash and filed as project-LICHEN-worker6-5r53-family follow-up bead (discovered-from this bead), left untouched per surgical scope. Committed.
